extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers and early-career biomedical/life-science scientists considering HHMI fellowship applications
extracted.subtask_short: HHMI Hanna H. Gray Fellows application
extracted.subtask_description: Information and eligibility rules for applying to the Howard Hughes Medical Institute (HHMI) Hanna H. Gray Fellows Program, a fellowship that funds postdoctoral training and potentially early independent faculty years. Includes applicant eligibility, eligible fields, and program features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted to join a lab in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must have been accepted to join a lab in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit eligibility requirement — applicants need an offer/acceptance to a U.S.-based laboratory at time of application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral experience limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Have no more than 24 months of postdoctoral research experience at the time of the application due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strict career-stage cutoff that determines eligibility based on accumulated postdoctoral time at the application deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-U.S. citizen degree requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-U.S. citizens and applicants with other nationalities must have a degree from a research institution in the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who are not U.S. citizens must hold a degree from a U.S. research institution to be eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible research focus / disciplines
rubrics_metrics.description: The competition is open to those dedicated to basic research from both doctoral and/or medical training paths in the biomedical and life science disciplines, including, but not limited to, plant biology, evolutionary biology, biophysics, chemical biology, biomedical engineering, and computational biology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program targets basic-research scientists across a broad set of life-science disciplines; the listed fields are examples and not necessarily exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible training paths
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to applicants from both doctoral and/or medical training paths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants may come from PhD or MD/medical training backgrounds, provided other eligibility criteria are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding purpose and potential extension to early faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows will receive funding for their postdoctoral training and, if eligible, in their early career years as independent faculty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support is intended to cover the postdoctoral phase and may extend into early independent faculty years for those who meet the program's conditions for such support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career development components
rubrics_metrics.description: The program includes opportunities for career development, including mentoring and active involvement in the HHMI scientific community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond monetary support, the program emphasizes mentoring and community integration as part of candidate development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application timing — deadline month
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are due in November (annual cycle); applicants should confirm the exact date on the HHMI site or program announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program categories / benefits (tags)
rubrics_metrics.description: Filed under: Postdoc Opportunities; U.S. Citizen; U.S. Citizen/ Permanent Resident; Non-U.S. Citizen; November; Science and Engineering; External; Research Expenses; Salary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These tags indicate the program is a postdoctoral opportunity open to various citizenship statuses and that funding likely addresses salary and research expenses (tags inferred from page filing). Confirm specifics on the official HHMI announcement.
